results.content: This study adopted a mixed-methods design to assess the reliability and validity of the "Chinese version of the Postoperative Anticoagulation Motivation Scale for Deep Vein Thrombosis Prophylaxis in Patients After Arthroplasty," based on Protection Motivation Theory, conducted sequentially in two stages. Given that the proposed scale consists of seven dimensions—risk perception, severity perception, internal rewards, external rewards, response efficacy, self-efficacy, and response cost—and that the dimension to which each item belongs was clear, the division of dimensions was based on the results of the exploratory factor analysis31. Several fit indices were used to evaluate the adequacy of the models, including normalized chi-square (CMIN/DF), root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA), parsimonious normative fit index (PNFI), relative fit index (RFI), incremental fit index (IFI), Tucker–Lewis fit index (TLI), and parsimony goodness-of-fit index (PGFI).The CFA results indicated that the motivational scale for anticoagulant use in DVT prophylaxis based on Protection Motivation Theory achieved an acceptable but not optimal fit for the five-factor model (Model 2), with RMSEA=0.076, IFI=0.896, and TLI=0.888 (Table 5).
